observations:
Torah 88 is a very brief, sealed teaching (the Rebbe himself calls it 'דברים סתומים וחתומים' — sealed and closed matters) that was also partially forgotten by the time it was recorded. Its bechina structure is therefore sparse and implicit rather than richly articulated.

The four packages proposed already cover all the explicit conceptual territory of the text:

1. Package 1 (Aveidot u-Malakh haShofar) covers the celestial recovery system — the angel, deputies, shofars, TRT, the joy of finding.
2. Package 2 (Taavah v'Avdan) covers the evil domain — desires, wicked, the loss they cause, pgam habrit.
3. Package 3 (Brachah v'Yirat Shamayim) covers the protective/rectifying spiritual stance — blessing, intention, fear of heaven, Elul kavanot, tikkun habrit.
4. Package 4 (Pri v'Koach haMoshekh) covers the neutral structural metaphor — the fruit, its drawing force, ripening, life-force.

The two sealed/forgotten items mentioned in para 10 — 'קינאת סופרים תרבה חכמה' and 'קשה מאד מאד להיות מקבל' — are insufficient to form independent packages. Each is mentioned as a single concept without any bechina connections stated. A new package requires 3+ concepts connected by explicit bechina language forming an independent domain. Neither of these isolated mentions meets that standard.

The connection to Elul (para 11) does not generate a new package either. The Rebbe states 'הכל אחד' — everything is one — explicitly indicating that the Elul dimension is not a separate domain but the overarching unity of the existing domains. The Elul content belongs within Package 3 as the תיקון dimension of the brachah/yirah domain.

Conclusion: The existing four packages are complete given the available text. Additional packages may have existed in the portions the Rebbe did not explain or that were forgotten, but these cannot be reconstructed from the surviving text.
